sharedDirection: Text-free cinematic Regency realism with a refined painterly finish, warm honey-gold daylight, welcoming period interiors, natural anatomy, no modern objects, no watermark, no readable writing, and a calm central-lower area for no more than two subtitle lines.

scenes.beat: Sir Walter finds comfort in the Baronetage.
scenes.prompt: Sir Walter Elliot sits beside a sunlit window at Kellynch Hall, absorbed in a large leather-bound baronetage; warm cream, honey and muted blue palette, flowers and polished wood, restrained subtitle-safe composition.

scenes.beat: The family register and genealogy are read aloud.
scenes.prompt: Warm close view of an antique genealogy and family register with decorative but illegible marks; Sir Walter in pleased profile beyond the book, bright Regency daylight and subtitle-safe lower middle.

scenes.beat: Sir Walter adds family notes and luxuriates in rank and appearance.
scenes.prompt: Sir Walter at a refined Regency writing desk adding family notes with a quill to a large old volume, proud and slightly comic without caricature, warm window light and tasteful period objects.

scenes.beat: Lady Elliot's character and the daughters' loss are remembered.
scenes.prompt: Kellynch Hall circa 1800 in warm late-afternoon light; Lady Elliot sits tenderly with her three young daughters while Sir Walter stands slightly apart, preoccupied with rank and appearance; bright dignified family memory, historically accurate and not melodramatic.

scenes.beat: Anne is overlooked by her father and sister but valued by Lady Russell.
scenes.prompt: Anne in her established dusty-blue dress stands quietly by a bright Kellynch window with a closed book; Lady Russell turns toward her with warmth while Sir Walter and Elizabeth converse together in the background and barely notice Anne.

scenes.beat: Elizabeth's confidence gives way to anxiety about age and marriage.
scenes.prompt: Elizabeth Elliot, handsome and poised at twenty-nine, closes the large family book with averted eyes and restrained disappointment in a luminous Kellynch drawing room; Sir Walter remains serenely self-satisfied near a mirror.

scenes.beat: Mr Elliot repeatedly disappoints the family's expectations and departs.
scenes.prompt: Elegant London townhouse entrance in spring circa 1801; a younger Elizabeth watches as well-dressed Mr Elliot departs toward a waiting horse carriage without looking back, while Sir Walter stands affronted beside her; warm wistful afternoon.

scenes.beat: Elizabeth nurses her resentment in the sameness of Kellynch life.
scenes.prompt: Elizabeth wears a restrained black mourning ribbon and sits alone beside the closed family book in Kellynch Hall, looking away with controlled resentment; grand warm room, static elegant life, gently melancholy but never dark.

scenes.beat: Sir Walter retreats into the Baronetage as debts accumulate.
scenes.prompt: Sir Walter proudly reads the Baronetage in his bright library while sealed bills and account papers lie ignored at the desk edge; Elizabeth stands nearby, newly aware and worried; subtle Austen irony and no readable marks.

scenes.beat: Father and daughter discuss retrenchment while protecting every luxury.
scenes.prompt: Sir Walter and Elizabeth seriously discuss retrenchment in a gracious Kellynch morning room surrounded by upholstery, flowers and comforts; she gestures toward a tiny insignificant saving and he recoils from meaningful sacrifice; warm, lightly comic realism.

scenes.beat: Lady Russell and Mr Shepherd are called to advise the family.
scenes.prompt: In Kellynch Hall's sunlit library, Sir Walter and Elizabeth receive practical advice from dignified Lady Russell and country solicitor Mr Shepherd around a polished table with a blank estate plan; thoughtful, warm and anticipatory conclusion.
